title: Deterministic D(S3) to D(Z3) phase-transition lifecycle preflight

scope.ungauge: Consume a verified abstract ungauge transition, open one cluster-owned D(Z3) region, and preserve an explicit supplied fusion outcome.
scope.measurement: Bind one current-round neutrality record to the preserved deterministic outcome and the active region.
scope.regauge: Terminate the region only after a neutral record and a matching abstract correct/regauge transition; keep a non-neutral region active.
not_in_scope: microscopic D(S3) gauging or ungauging circuit
derivation of the supplied fusion outcome
measurement noise or repeated parity inference
schedule performance, threshold, or fault tolerance

invariants: one active ungauged region exists per cluster
only an ungauge transition from D(S3) or boundary to D(Z3) may open a region
the supplied fusion outcome is unchanged across the labelled phase transition
neutrality records are current-round, owner-bound, region-bound, and consistent with the deterministic supplied outcome
non-neutral deferral leaves the ungauged region active
correct/regauge requires a recorded neutral outcome and terminates the absorber exactly once
all phase lifecycle events are deterministic and causally ordered

verified_cases: ungauging opens one owned active region and preserves the supplied fusion outcome exactly
a neutral current-round parity record permits one correct/re-gauge termination
a non-neutral record keeps the ungauged region active
a deterministic parity record inconsistent with the preserved outcome is rejected
invalid transition order and duplicate region creation are rejected
a public abstract schedule trace drives ungauge, measurement, and re-gauge without truth access

claim_boundary: This contract tests only a deterministic phase-labelled lifecycle around the already abstract schedule. Passing it will not constitute a microscopic D(S3) reproduction or evidence for performance, threshold, or fault tolerance.
next_gate: Implement causal detector-cluster construction from observation records, including age, extent, separation, and absorber-link candidates, so the schedule no longer receives hand-assembled clusters; keep microscopic/noisy claims excluded.
